messages.subject: continuity in the development of breedR
messages.subject_clean: continuity in the development of breedR
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I have been the main (and almost only) developer of breedR for a few years now. As some of you might know, I have switched jobs, from a postdoctoral position at INRA (where breedR was conceived by Leopoldo Sanchez) to a permanent position as a Biostatistician at Cirad.

I think it is fair to keep you informed regarding the prospects of breedR.

Cirad is a different research institution also concerned by agricultural modeling and by quantitative genetics to some extent. That means that my domains of interest here are close enough to justify some investment of time on breedR.

On the other hand, I cannot consider involving myself directly in the development of new functionalities. _But_ if someone decides to invest resources in further development this person will have all my support. This includes guidance on how breedR's code is organized (there is only little documentation on this), guidance on the workflows for development, testing and releasing and help on where to start making changes. I am aware of some future plans in this regard, but nothing concrete so far.

In summary, I will keep:

- giving support on the use of breedR by reading this mailing list, answering questions, fixing bugs and maintaining the code up to date with respect to PROGSF90, R and other dependencies

- fixing or improving some small usability issues which do not involve too much time

- improving the documentation, guides and use cases

- releasing new versions when necessary and keeping the repository functional

- giving technical support to whoever decides to invest resources in further development

I hope breedR will continue to be a useful tool for you, and I look forward to hear from you soon.

Best wishes

ƒacu.-
